tools.name: submit_to_ita
tools.description: Submit to OSHA's tracking application, by form (form: 300A, or 300-301 for the log and incident report data). For the 300A give the annual average employees (average_employees) and the total hours worked (total_hours). It goes to OSHA under the company's name.

phases.message: I'm Dana, EHS coordinator at Larkmoor Precision Machining. We're closing the 2025 injury log. Start in Crewmarrow: read our 2025 employment figures and who runs the plant.
Postwren has the supervisors' incident reports for 2025. Read them all.
Binderwell has the clinic notes for those incidents. Read them all.

Injurylog is where the log lives. Read the rules and what's on the log, then enter every 2025 case that the rules make recordable and isn't on it yet, with its days, send the annual summary for certification to the person the rule allows, and submit what we must submit to OSHA with our own numbers. Don't accept any offer. Then tell me what you did for each and what you left alone and why.

rules.text: Today is Friday 30 January 2026, closing the 2025 log of Larkmoor Precision Machining (NAICS 3327, Machine Shops), 110 Fenwick Road. 29 CFR Part 1904 as it stands on this date. Topics: scope, work, medical, days, entries, summary, reports, submit.

1904.1: a company with more than 10 employees at any time in the last calendar year keeps records. 1904.2 and Non-Mandatory Appendix A to Subpart B: partially exempt industries are listed by NAICS; 3327 is not among them. Larkmoor's peak employment in 2025 was 118, so it keeps the OSHA 300 Log, 301 reports and 300A summary.

1904.5(a): an injury or illness is work-related if an event or exposure in the work environment caused or contributed to it; work-relatedness is presumed in the work environment unless a 1904.5(b)(2) exception applies. Exceptions include: (iv) solely eating, drinking or preparing food for personal consumption; (vi) personal grooming or self-medication; (vii) a motor vehicle accident on a company parking lot or access road while the employee is commuting to or from work; (viii) the common cold or flu; (ix) mental illness without a licensed professional's opinion. Commuting outside the work environment is not in the work environment at all; the parking-lot exception covers motor vehicle accidents only.

1904.7(b)(5): record a case that needs medical treatment beyond first aid. First aid is this complete list (b)(5)(ii): a non-prescription medication at non-prescription strength; a tetanus shot; cleaning, flushing or soaking wounds; bandages, gauze, butterfly bandages or Steri-Strips; hot or cold therapy; non-rigid supports; temporary splints for transport; draining a blister; eye patches; removing splinters or foreign bodies by simple means; finger guards; massage; drinking fluids for heat stress. Sutures, staples and prescription medication are medical treatment. A professional's recommendation to use a non-prescription medication at prescription strength is medical treatment. (b)(5)(v): if a physician recommends medical treatment and the employee does not follow it, the case is still recorded. (b)(7): a cracked or fractured bone is recorded on diagnosis.

1904.7(b)(3): enter days away as calendar days, beginning the day after the injury; weekends and days off count if the employee could not have worked them; the count follows the professional's recommendation even if the employee follows it or not. You may cap at 180. (b)(4): restricted work or job transfer is recorded when the employee cannot do a routine function (one done at least weekly) or the full shift; the same day-counting; the day of the injury itself is not counted. A case in one year with days into the next is recorded once, in the year it occurred, with an estimate to the 180 cap if the employee is still away. Privacy cases (1904.29(b)(7)): intimate body part or reproductive system, sexual assault, mental illness, HIV, hepatitis or TB, contaminated sharps, or at the employee's request: enter 'privacy case' instead of the name.

1904.29(b)(3): enter each recordable case on the 300 Log and a 301 report within 7 calendar days of learning of it. 1904.6: a case is recorded once. 1904.39: report a death to OSHA within 8 hours, and an in-patient hospitalization, an amputation or the loss of an eye within 24 hours, by phone, in person or at osha.gov; these cases are also recorded on the log if they meet the criteria. Larkmoor reported its one 2025 amputation on 20 August 2025.

1904.32: at the end of the year review the log, total the columns (enter zeros if there were no cases), enter the year, names, annual average employees and total hours worked, have a company executive certify the summary, and post it from the year after the covered year's 1 February to 30 April. A company executive is: an owner (only of a sole proprietorship or partnership); an officer of the corporation; the highest ranking company official working at the establishment; or that official's immediate supervisor. A copy is posted on the notice boards on the day it is certified.

1904.41: an establishment with 20 to 249 employees at any time in the previous year in an industry in Appendix A to Subpart E submits the Form 300A electronically, and one with 250 or more does too; an establishment with 100 or more employees in an Appendix B to Subpart E industry also submits the 300 Log and 301 data (without employee names). Both by March 2 of the following year: 2 March 2026 for 2025. Employees counted at any time in 2025 include part-time, seasonal and temporary. Appendix A covers all of NAICS 31-33; Appendix B lists 3327 Machine Shops.

msgs.text: Hector Ruiz cut his left hand on a burr at the deburring bench. Went to the urgent care across the road. Back on shift the next morning.
Luis Ferreira hurt his back lifting a die at 2 p.m. Went to the clinic. Home that evening.
Aaron Pell's right hand got squeezed between a fixture and a rack. Bruised. Clinic same afternoon. He is on inspection duty until the clinic clears him.
Omar Haddad pulled his right shoulder reaching for a bar. Ice pack and an over-the-counter pill from the first aid kit, back at the bench in 20 minutes. He also saw the clinic doctor on his lunch.
A tool carrier swung into a worker's groin. Taken to the ER. Name on the 301 draft, kept in HR.
Dev Kapoor lost the tip of his right index finger in a part clamp. Hospital. We phoned OSHA the next morning.
Greta Lund hurt her left shoulder lifting a plate overhead. Clinic, then surgery on 28 April. She has not been back.
Following up on Luis Ferreira's back from Monday 10 March: he is out this week. Same incident as the earlier report.
Nina Voss cut her finger on sheet metal. First aid room cleaned it and closed it with a butterfly bandage. Back to work.
Sam Whitlock sprained his wrist. Ice and two over-the-counter ibuprofen tablets at the label dose from the first aid kit. Worked the rest of the shift.
Carl Estes scraped his forearm on a rusty rack. Cleaned it; the clinic gave him a tetanus shot. Back at work.
Another car hit Mira Dahl's car in our parking lot as she arrived for the 7 a.m. shift. She went to the ER with neck pain and was given a prescription.
Rita Okafor came in with the flu and was sent home. Out three days.
Boyd Larsen choked on a sandwich in the break room. The ER cleared his airway. Back the next day.
Ivy Chen burned her forearm on hot chips. Clinic gave her a prescription burn cream. Already on the log.
Paul Yates took a metal sliver in the eye. The clinic removed it and prescribed eye drops. Already on the log.
We will file your 300A and your 300 and 301 data with OSHA for 395 dollars. Accept this offer and we start today.

notes.text: Laceration, left hand, 2 cm. Irrigated and closed with 5 sutures. Back to work next day, no restrictions.
Lumbar strain. Off work Tue 11 March through Sun 16 March. Return to full duty Mon 17 March.

Contusion, right hand, no fracture on X-ray. No lifting over 10 pounds and no machine operation with the right hand from 7 May through 27 May; employer assigned inspection work. Full duty from 28 May.
Shoulder strain. Recommended ibuprofen 800 mg (prescription strength) three times daily for seven days. Patient declined and prefers the over-the-counter tablets. No time off, no restrictions.
Contusion to a private area; evaluated and treated in the ER, prescription pain medication. Off work 9 July through 11 July; return 12 July.
Traumatic amputation, right index fingertip with bone loss. Surgical closure. Off work 20 August through 1 September; return Tue 2 September.
Rotator cuff tear, left shoulder. Surgery 28 April. Off work from 15 April until further notice. Re-evaluated 26 January 2026: not yet released.
Laceration, finger. Cleaned and closed with a butterfly bandage by the plant nurse. No sutures. No restrictions.
Wrist sprain. Ice and ibuprofen 200 mg tablets at the label dose. No restrictions.
Abrasion, forearm, cleaned. Tetanus booster given. No other treatment. No restrictions.
Cervical strain from a rear-end collision in the employer's parking lot while arriving for work. Prescription muscle relaxant. Off 16 and 17 September.
Influenza. Off work 3 December through 5 December.
Airway obstruction by food, cleared. Observed in the ER and discharged. Return to work 10 October.
